claim: Current Nix manual (2.35.2 nix.conf): 'on Linux, builds run in private PID, mount, network, IPC and UTS namespaces', sandbox defaults to true on Linux, and the only network-namespace exception is fixed-output derivations; plain loopback TCP inside the sandbox requires no special permission, while setuid/capability programs (needed for userspace netns setup) are unavailable unless bind-mounted.
stance_target: gap-04: authoritative manual confirmation of the netns + default-on sandbox semantics the harness relies on; also explains why the harness needs no escape hatch
quoted_support: In addition, on Linux, builds run in private PID, mount, network, IPC and UTS namespaces to isolate them from other processes in the system (except that fixed-output derivations do not run in private network namespace to ensure they can access the network).
